title: Live Telecast of 24th Instalment of PM-KISAN Scheme Held at ICAR-NIBSM - www.pib.gov.in
text:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Live Telecast of 24th Instalment of PM-KISAN Scheme Held at ICAR-NIBSM Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 6:12PM by PIB Raipur The live telecast of the national programme marking the release of the 24th instalment of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme was organised at the ICAR–National Institute of Biotic Stress Management, Raipur. Farmers at the institute witnessed the programme held at Banaskantha, Gujarat, where the Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, released the financial assistance directly into the bank accounts of farmers across the country. Before the live telecast and the Prime Minister’s address, Director of the Institute, Dr. P. K. Rai, addressed the farmers. He highlighted the objectives and significance of the PM-KISAN scheme and elaborated on various initiatives undertaken by the Government of India for agricultural development and farmers’ welfare. He encouraged farmers to avail themselves of the benefits of government schemes and adopt scientific agricultural practices to enhance farm productivity and sustainability. Addressing the nation from Banaskantha, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi described farmers as a strong pillar of a developed India and reaffirmed the government's commitment to agriculture and farmers' welfare. He emphasised that the PM-KISAN scheme has become an integral part of the lives of millions of farming families and that financial assistance through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) is helping farmers meet their agricultural and household needs. On the occasion, Joint Director of the Institute, Dr. Pankaj Sharma, interacted with the farmers and discussed strategies for better agricultural planning for the forthcoming Rabi season. He particularly emphasised crop diversification and advised farmers to integrate pulses and oilseed crops into their existing cropping systems, diversify traditional cropping patterns and make efficient use of available agricultural resources. Approximately 270 farmers from eight nearby villages participated enthusiastically in the programme, including 41 women and 229 men. Farmers from Bitia, Kurra, Pachri, Barode, Budera, Beltukri, Madhai, Murra and Bhainsa villages attended the event. Local representatives, including Shri Santosh Kurre, Sarpanch of Beltukri village; Shri Bhuvneshwar Khunte from Kurra village; and Shri Dushyant Sahu from Bitia village, were also present. The programme witnessed active participation and enthusiastic interaction among farmers. The event provided an important platform to disseminate information about various farmer-welfare initiatives of the Government of India and to promote scientific agricultural technologies, crop diversification and sustainable farming practices. Scientists, officers, and other staff members of the Institute were also present. The programme was effectively coordinated and conducted by Dr. K. C.
